battle.name: 蒙古平李璮之戰
battle.brief: 中統三年（1262）春，紅袄軍首領李璮在山東舉兵反元，據濟南、青州等城，並遣使向南宋求援。忽必烈命史天澤總兵討平，蒙軍以騎兵分割包圍、封鎖漕運糧道，並以石砲轟擊濟南城樓，圍城數月後守軍潰散，李璮突圍南走終被部將縛送大都。卡上的配重投石車正是決定城防崩壞的攻城器械。

kit.name: 配重投石車
kit.history: 長臂配重把石頭甩過城牆。工程比攻城武器更早決定勝負。

countries: 1262年的山東，衝突的一方是元朝中央直轄的討伐軍：蒙古本部的騎兵萬戶為突擊主力，漢軍千戶所屬的步卒與攻城砲手負責結營、攻城與器械操作，各地調集的守城部隊、隨軍工匠與牛馬隊伍構成後勤。指揮系統上，忽必烈中統三年下詔，命中書右丞相史天澤總兵，以河南行省之權節制各路；張禧、董文炳等漢軍將領分道進攻，廉希憲則奉命宣撫山東、處理善後。地方一線仍保留金末以來的軍鎮與稅務機構，李全留下、改編為「忠孝軍」的紅袄軍是李璮可以倚仗的班底，起義發動後即以此為骨架。起義方一面是李璮整合的紅袄軍舊部、新附鄉兵與地方豪強武裝，據濟南、青州、密州等城，兼行騎兵游擊與堅城自守，並遣使向南宋求援。南宋朝廷把此事視為牽制北方的契機，議有接應之策但援軍終未及時北上，起義軍因此陷於孤立。表面看是地方叛亂，實則是元廷整併漢地軍鎮、推行直接稅收的一次正面測試。
countriesEn: The clash in Shandong in 1262 was fought between the centrally controlled army of the Yuan dynasty and the Red Coat insurgents under Li Tan. On the government side the field force was built around the cavalry units of the Mongol banners, with Han Chinese infantry and artillery crews from the Han army thousand-household system responsible for entrenching, siege work and the handling of engines, while regional garrisons, craftsmen and the ox and camel trains formed the tail of the column. In the chain of command Kublai issued the decree in the third year of the Zhongtong era, gave the overall command to the chancellor Shi Tianze with the authority of the Henan branch of the Secretariat, and set Zhang Xi, Dong Wenbing and other Han commanders to advance by separate routes, while Lian Xixian was sent to pacify Shandong and settle the aftermath. On the local side the institutions inherited from the late Jin survived, and the Red Coat corps left behind by Li Quan and reorganised as the Zhongxiao army was the skeleton on which Li Tan built. The insurgents were Li Tan's own veteran Red Coats, newly attached village levies and the private retainers of local strongmen; they held Jinan, Qingzhou and Mizhou, combining mounted harassment with stubborn defence, and sent envoys to the Southern Song for help. The Song court saw the revolt as a chance to pin down the north, discussed a response, yet no relief army reached Shandong in time, so the insurgents fought isolated. On the surface this was a local rebellion; in substance it was a direct test of the Yuan court's attempt to absorb the Han commanderies and to take the taxes into its own hands.
people: 李璮，字德輝，山東濰州人，紅袄軍首領李全之弟或族弟。他早年隨兄起兵於山東，金朝覆亡後率眾歸附蒙古，靠括戶與稅課維持一支相當可觀的武裝；兄長於1236年死後，濟南一帶的軍權與財源落到他手上。1262年他率先起兵、殺害蒙古官員、據城自立，是這場衝突的直接決策者；他最關鍵的兩次判斷，一是據守濟南等待宋援，二是最後決定夜間突圍南走，卻因此落進蒙軍預設的截擊。忽必烈是另一端的決策者，他中統三年春下詔討平，命史天澤統兵，批准分路進兵、封鎖漕運與糧道的方案；事後又聽取廉希憲與史天澤的意見，减免山東賦稅、招撫流民、整編忠孝軍，令官府直收稅課。史天澤是漢人世侯出身的中書右丞相，主張圍城斷糧而不急於強攻，並屢請勿濫殺百姓，是這場戰役在政策面的主要把關人。張禧與董文炳都是漢軍名將，1262年奉命分道進兵，攻城與追擊的實務多出於此二人之手，其中董文炳此後轉戰攻宋，成為襄陽戰線的主將，把山東得來的攻城經驗帶到更大的會戰裡。南宋方面沒有留下具名的援軍統帥，接應之議屢成空談。
peopleEn: Li Tan, courtesy name Dehui, was a native of Weizhou in Shandong and the brother or cousin-brother of Li Quan, the first chief of the Red Coats. He had risen with his brother in the Red Coat rising of the late Jin, and after the dynasty fell in 1234 he brought his men over to the Mongols and kept a considerable armed following alive on the proceeds of household registration and tax farming; when Li Quan died in 1236 the military power and the revenue of the Jinan area passed into his hands. It was Li Tan who struck first in 1262, killing Mongol officials and declaring himself in the occupied cities, and he was the direct decision maker of the whole affair. His two crucial judgements were to hold Jinan and wait for Song aid, and then, as a last measure, to break out south by night, a move that carried him straight into the interception the Mongols had prepared. On the other side Kublai was the decision maker: in the spring of the third year of Zhongtong he issued the decree to suppress the revolt, appointed Shi Tianze to command, and approved the plan of attacking by separate routes while sealing the river transport and the supply roads; afterwards he took the advice of Lian Xixian and Shi Tianze, remitted the taxes of Shandong, called for the return of the refugees, reorganised the Zhongxiao army and had the government collect the taxes directly. Shi Tianze, chancellor and a hereditary Han commander, argued for strangling the city by supply rather than storming it, and repeatedly asked that the population not be massacred; he was the principal guardian of policy in this campaign. Zhang Xi and Dong Wenbing, both famous Han commanders, were sent by separate routes in 1262 and carried out most of the practical work of siege and pursuit, and Dong Wenbing later turned to the war against the Song, becoming a leading commander on the Xiangyang front and carrying the siege experience gained in Shandong into far larger engagements. On the Song side no commander is named for the relief force; the project of intervention was talked over and repeatedly came to nothing.
kits: 兵器卡上的配重投石車，是十二世紀已在西歐與地中海世界用於攻城的機械：長臂末端裝載石彈，臂尾以重箱配重，靠釋放配重把石彈甩過城牆，射程遠、單發撞擊力大，代價是每次發射都要人工重新上弦與复位，射速遠低於弩砲，轉場極慢，必須隨軍伐木造架並編入工匠隊。蒙古統治下的華北並不陌生的攻城主力是「砲」（泛指投石機），既有華夏固有的牽拉式霹靂車，也有配重式；配重式的技術經中亞與波斯工程師傳入，1271至1272年隨蒙軍攻宋，最先用於襄陽、樊城之圍，正是這一脈的頂點。1262年濟南之圍時，元軍手中的投石器已足以在城外成排展開，砲擊城樓、屋頂與城頭掩體，與壕溝填塞、穴地道進逼、雲梯搭攻城頭同時進行；火藥兵器如毒煙火砲與震天雷也已出現，但用量仍少，主要用於城門爆破。除攻城器械外，蒙古騎兵用鋼弦反曲弓配骨石箭頭放出箭幕，人員裝備以皮甲或鎖子甲為主，配短刀與長矛；運營方面靠輜重車隊、牛馬駝隊輸送石料與糧食，投石機的木料多就地徵集。
kitsEn: The card shows a counterweight trebuchet, a machine already used for siege in western Europe and the Mediterranean world of the twelfth century: a long arm carries the stone at one end, a heavy counterweight hangs at the other, and the release of that weight flings the stone over the wall. Its range is long and the impact of a single shot is heavy, but the price is that the machine must be wound up and reset by hand for every shot; the rate of fire is far below that of a crossbow engine, the engine is painfully slow to move, and it has to be built from timber felled on the spot and served by a crew of engineers. The besiegers of North China under Mongol rule were no strangers to the siege engine, for the pao, used as a general term for the stone thrower, was already their principal tool: some were the traction type inherited from the Chinese, the Huihui pao of later fame was the counterweight type brought in through Central Asia and Persia, and it was used at Xiangyang and Fancheng in 1271 and 1272, the high point of that line of development. At the siege of Jinan in 1262 the Yuan army already had stone throwers in numbers sufficient to be ranged in rows outside the walls; they battered the towers, the roofs and the fighting platforms, working together with the filling of the ditch, the driving of mines under the wall and the ladders brought up to the parapet. Gunpowder devices such as the smoke bomb and the thunder crash bomb were also present, but in small quantities, and were mostly used against gates. Outside the siege train, the Mongol horse archers used laminated recurve bows of horn and sinew with bone or stone heads, and the men themselves wore leather or mail with a short sword and a spear; on the logistics side, ox carts, pack animals and camel trains moved the stone and the grain, and the timber for the throwers was levied locally.
tactics: 蒙軍的作戰仍帶著草原軍隊的老習慣：先以哨騎廣泛偵察，再以數路騎兵高速迂迴，把守軍外援與糧道先行切斷，最後才合圍城下。濟南之圍最見特色的是困而不攻：蒙軍封住黃河與濟水沿線的漕運、斷絕城郊村寨的糧源，寧可數月不動，也不肯在城牆下硬撞；同時在城南預設截擊部隊，等的就是守軍出城的一刻。攻城手段是分層的：先用石砲在遠距離削平城頭與樓櫓，再以壕溝填塞、穴地掘進把盾牆推到城下，配合雲梯與撞車；此外還不斷遣使入城招撫將士，散布赦免與厚賞之令，希望從內部瓦解。守方的李璮以濟南為樞紐，城周村寨互為犄角，派遊騎反覆襲擾蒙軍側後與運糧隊，藉此拖慢合圍，並遣使南下求援爭取時間。糧道斷絕之後他仍作持久打算，直到守軍飢疲、援兵不至，才選擇夜間突圍南走，結果在途中被蒙軍咬住，隊伍沿途潰散，殘部終被部下捆縛送京。後來襄陽之役的配重砲連射加掘壕圍城，可以看作這套辦法的放大與成熟。
tacticsEn: The Mongol conduct of the campaign still followed the habits of a steppe army: wide reconnaissance by outriders first, then several bodies of cavalry moving at speed to turn the flank, cutting off the relief column and the supply route before anything else, and only then closing in on the city. The siege of Jinan showed most clearly what can be called a siege without an assault. The Mongols sealed the river transport along the Yellow River and the Ji, cut the grain coming in from the villages around the walls, and preferred to stand still for months rather than smash themselves against the masonry; at the same time they posted a force to the south of the city to wait for the moment the garrison would break out. The siege methods were layered: stone throwers at long range to level the parapet and the towers, then filled ditches and driven mines to push the shields up to the wall, with ladders and battering rams in support; and alongside the artillery, envoys were constantly sent into the city to offer terms to the officers and men and to spread promises of pardon and reward, hoping to break the defence from within. On the other side Li Tan made Jinan his pivot, with the villages around the walls interlocking as mutual support, and sent out light horse to harry the Mongol flanks and their grain convoys, in order to slow the closing net, while envoys went south to seek Song help and gain time. Even after the supply was cut he still planned to hold out, and only when the garrison was hungry and no relief came did he choose to break out south by night; the column was caught on the road, scattered on the way, and the remnant was finally bound by his own men and sent to the capital. The counterweight batteries firing in series over dug approaches at Xiangyang were the enlargement and the refinement of this same method.
data: 可核對的數字有限，且多帶誇張。起兵時間一般記為元中統三年（1262）春，二月至三月之間起兵；濟南被攻破或迫降在同年秋，約九十月；李璮被押送京師並處決，則在中統四年（1263）初。兵力方面，李璮一方常被寫成十餘萬，合理的估計是核心騎兵數千、步卒與鄉兵合計數萬；蒙古方面集中兵數在數萬至十萬級別之間，含蒙古騎兵、漢軍步卒與隨軍夫役，史籍所載常把後勤與援軍一併計入。城防與距離方面，濟南城牆周長以數十里計，護城壕不止一道；濟南至中都（燕京）約四百公里，濟南至楚州（淮安）沿驛道亦約四百公里，一支飢疲的突圍部隊走完全程需數十日。器械方面，一座配重投石車每日可發數十發，圍城數月意味著要運石數萬斤、伐木數百株造砲架與雲梯；蒙軍沿途還要維持數萬匹馬的飼料與水源，黃河、濟水沿線的漕運船隊則是糧秣的骨幹。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked are few, and most of them are inflated. The rising is generally dated to the spring of the third year of the Zhongtong era of the Yuan, 1262, somewhere between the second and the third month; the fall of Jinan, whether by storm or by surrender, is placed in the autumn of the same year, around the ninth or tenth month; and the escort of Li Tan to the capital and his execution belong to the beginning of the fourth year of Zhongtong, 1263. On numbers of men, Li Tan's side is habitually written up as more than a hundred thousand; a reasonable estimate is a core of several thousand horsemen with infantry and village levies together numbering in the tens of thousands. The force Mongol concentration is a matter of degrees, from tens of thousands to a hundred thousand, counting Mongol horse, Han infantry and the train that moved with them, since the chronicles tend to fold the logistics and the reinforcing columns into the same total. On fortifications and distances, the circuit of the walls of Jinan is given in tens of li, and the ditch was more than a single line; from Jinan to the Central Capital at Dadu is about four hundred kilometres, and from Jinan to Chuzhou at Huai'an along the post road is again about four hundred, so that a hungry column making the whole run would need tens of days. On the engines, a single counterweight trebuchet could throw perhaps several dozen stones a day, and a siege lasting months implies the moving of tens of thousands of jin of stone and the felling of several hundred trees for the frames and the ladders; the army also had to feed and water tens of thousands of horses along the road, with the river transport on the Yellow River and the Ji forming the backbone of the supply.
cause: 紅袄軍的前身是金末山東以紅巾為號的起義群眾，既抗金也抗官府；金朝於1234年覆亡後，這些武裝沒有被解散，而是改換旗號，改以蒙古的名義繼續佔據地方，靠括戶與稅課養兵，實行半獨立的割據。李全死後，這套由家族與軍頭控制的軍鎮與稅源落到李璮手上，成為他一切行動的依託。忽必烈於1260年即位後推行漢法，罷諸路括戶、禁治貪官、減省賦稅，並令官府直理稅課，山東又是減賦與改制的先行之地；這意味著李璮的財源被削、兵員被吸走、忠孝軍隨時可能被整編或拆散，他因而感到生存威脅，遂先發制人，聚眾殺官、據城自立，對外則以聯宋為名爭取呼應。時局同樣有利於起義：蒙哥汗死後，忽必烈與阿里不哥爭奪汗位，北方邊防鬆動，山東一線的兵力調度尚未完成。山東連年水旱與蝗災、稅負與盜匪並存，也讓鄉民願意附從，起義得以迅速擴大。
causeEn: The Red Coats grew out of the rising of the red-hooded multitude in late Jin Shandong, which had fought both the dynasty and its own officials. When the Jin fell in 1234 these armed groups were not disbanded; they changed their banners, continued to hold the country in the name of the Mongols, and maintained their troops on the proceeds of household registration and tax farming, in effect a half independent separatism. After the death of Li Quan this system of garrisons and revenue, controlled by a family and its military captains, passed into Li Tan's hands and became the support of everything he did. After his accession in 1260 Kublai pursued Chinese methods of government: cancelling household registration throughout the provinces, punishing corrupt officials, remitting taxes and having the government collect the revenues directly, and Shandong was among the first provinces where the reduction and the reform were carried out. For Li Tan this meant his income being cut, his soldiers being drawn away, and the Zhongxiao army liable at any moment to be reorganised or broken up. Faced with that threat to his existence he struck first, gathering men, killing officials and setting himself up in the occupied cities, while seeking a response abroad under the banner of alliance with the Song. The state of the world favoured the rising as well: after the death of Möngke, Kublai and Ariq Böke were contesting the khanship, the northern frontier was slack, and the redeployment of troops along the Shandong line had not been completed. Successive floods, droughts and locusts in Shandong, together with heavy taxes and banditry, inclined the villagers to join, and the rising spread quickly.
impact: 直接後果是紅袄軍作為武裝割據勢力被連根拔除：李璮伏誅，忠孝軍編制取消或整編，附從將士或降或散，山東因戰亂出現大量流亡，州縣一度近乎空虛。元廷在善後上改弦更張，由官府直收稅課，罷括戶，减免賦稅、招撫流民、興修水利，史天澤與廉希憲都主張以安民為先，並把軍隊屯田與軍糧供應一併整頓。這套做法後來被推廣到漢地其他新征服地區，成為蒙古政權長期統治中原的基本政策取向，其意義不亞於任何一場會戰。軍事的傳承更為深遠：山東之圍積累的砲兵編制、掘壕封鎖與糧道戰術，後來原封不動地搬到1270年代的襄陽戰役，而配重投石車（回回砲）在那裡以最大規模投入，成為壓垮宋軍城防的關鍵器械；可以說，李璮之亂既解決了元朝的後方問題，也把元朝的攻城技術推到臨界點。對南宋而言，這次接應落空，等於錯失一次牽制北方的機會，也顯示宋蒙之間並無有效協調。
impactEn: The immediate consequence was the uprooting of the Red Coats as an armed separatist force. Li Tan was executed, the Zhongxiao army was disbanded or reorganised, those who had followed him surrendered or scattered, and the war left Shandong with a great displacement of population, some prefectures and counties reduced to near emptiness. The Yuan court changed its tune in the settlement: taxes were collected by the government, household registration was cancelled, levies were remitted, refugees were called back and waterworks were repaired; both Shi Tianze and Lian Xixian pressed for the population to be settled first, and the organisation of garrison farms and the issue of military grain were reformed at the same time. This approach was later extended to the other newly conquered districts of the Han country and became the basic policy of Mongol rule over the Chinese plains, and its importance was not less than that of any pitched battle. The military inheritance was even deeper. The artillery organisation, the sieges by dug approaches and the war on supply lines worked out in Shandong were carried over unchanged to the campaign against Xiangyang in the 1270s, where the counterweight trebuchet, the Huihui pao, was deployed on the largest scale yet and became the instrument that broke the Song defences; in that sense the revolt of Li Tan both settled the problem of the Yuan rear and pushed Yuan siegecraft to its limit. For the Southern Song, the failure of the relief was the loss of a chance to pin the north, and it showed once again that no effective coordination existed between Song and Mongol.
result: 經過大半年拉鋸，濟南守軍在糧道斷絕、援兵不至之後崩潰，李璮於1262年秋冬間夜間突圍南走，隊伍在途中被蒙軍追擊截斷，部眾星散，本人終被部下捆縛送京；1263年初他在中都被處決，據傳屍身被肢解示眾於諸王營前，附叛者亦多被究治。南宋的援軍最終沒有出現在山東。判定上，這場平叛以起義軍的徹底失敗告終：紅袄軍時代結束，濟南一帶由朝廷直轄，山東的稅制、兵制與官制都回到中央控制之下。史料仍有不確定處：濟南最後是城破還是守將出降，兩種記載並存；蒙軍與起義軍的兵數多為誇大；本戰的確切交戰日期只能由《元史·世祖紀》與《元史·李璮傳》的零散記載推估。此外，卡上的配重投石車與濟南之圍所用器械的具體型制（牽拉式拋石機抑或配重式）在原始記載中並未細分，較宜從技術譜系與攻城史的角度理解，而不宜當作某一次發射的實物記載。
resultEn: After a struggle of rather more than half a year, the garrison of Jinan gave way once its supply was cut and no relief came. Li Tan broke out south by night in the late autumn and winter of 1262, the column was cut off and harried on the road, the ranks scattered, and the man himself was finally bound by his own followers and sent to the capital; in the beginning of 1263 he was executed at Dadu, and it is said that his body was quartered and displayed before the camp of the Mongol princes, while those implicated were widely punished. Song relief never appeared in Shandong. On any judgement the suppression ended in the complete defeat of the insurgents: the age of the Red Coats was over, the Jinan area returned to direct rule, and the taxation, the military system and the administration of Shandong all came back under central control. The record remains uncertain in places. Whether Jinan at last fell by storm or was surrendered by its commandant is told both ways; the numbers of men on both sides are largely exaggerated; and the exact dates of the fighting can only be reconstructed from scattered entries in the Yüan shih. As for the counterweight trebuchet on the card, the original sources do not separate the traction from the counterweight type in the engines actually used at Jinan, and the machine is better read through the history of siegecraft and the genealogy of the type than taken as a record of any single shot.
